why.pressures: It raised an army against the Third Empire and watched a battlemage break it with one spell. It distrusts magic first and outsiders second.

places.name: Threewater

why.founding: Where the western feeder from eastern Blackwood meets the lake system, a market grew for everyone unwilling to pay Blackrose's gate toll.
why.siteAdvantages: A river junction with firm banks on three sides and enough water for laden hulls in every season but the driest.
why.occupantsMotive: It exists to be cheaper than Blackrose, and its whole civic life is organised around staying that way.
why.pressures: Blackrose has twice sent 'inspectors'; the town has twice paid them and continued.
why.wouldChangeIf: An enforced toll here would collapse the market back into the city within two years.

hardConstraints: a junction of navigable waters, or a road crossing
inland of the coast plain, on the Blackrose lake system

preferences.neighbourRelation: the western feeder's junction, a half-day inland of Blackrose

vibe.silhouette: A flat grid of open-sided shed roofs along a river junction, with not one wall, gate or tower in the whole outline.
vibe.palette: Shed timber, grain sack, brown river.
vibe.materials: Bamboo and mud-mother frames with shed roofing over open sides, market canvas, plank scales at every stall, one landmark scale-house; deliberately nothing defensible.
vibe.signatureFeature: A grid of open-sided trading sheds along a river junction, each with its own scale, and not one wall or gate anywhere in the town.
vibe.condition: Cheap, new and constantly rebuilt; nothing here is meant to last.
vibe.approach: You arrive along the river and there is no edge to the town. The sheds simply start.
vibe.senses: Weighing all day, a hundred scales and a hundred arguments; grain dust; river; the total absence of any gate-bell.
